title: Parsing nested `calc()` that contains a `var()` takes exponential time
impact: Parse time doubles per nesting level of math functions (calc/min/...) around a var() in any typed property. Humans essentially never nest this deep; reporter says a variable-substitution tool generated ~250 levels and hung. No reactions; same-day batch. Main concern is denial of service: a ~300-byte declaration stalls a build or a service that runs lightningcss on CSS it does not control (depth 20 ~4.5 s, depth 25 would be minutes, 250 effectively forever). Present since at least 1.14.0.
code: src/values/calc.rs: Calc::parse_value (try_parse(Self::parse) fails because of var(), then `V::parse` re-parses the same math function via its own Calc<V> path)
summary: When a nested math function fails to parse as Calc<V> (here because of var()), Calc::parse_value falls through to V::parse, which parses the same function again as Calc<V> and fails the same way. Each level doubles the work, so nesting depth d costs ~2^d. The declaration then falls back to unparsed tokens, so the output is correct, only slow.
repro: triage/sweep/1389-repro.mjs (depth 17, 100 ms budget; ~0.5 s release / ~6 s debug when broken). Timings (separate process per depth, 20 s timeout), `.x{width:calc(...calc(var(--x) - 1px)... - 1px)}`: 1.33.0 release d5 0.4 ms, d10 2.6 ms, d15 150 ms, d20 4487 ms; master (debug binding) d5 1.9 ms, d10 40 ms, d15 1479 ms, d20 >20 s. min(var(--x), 1px) nesting the same (1.33.0 d18 1115 ms). Controls flat (<3 ms at d20): no var(), the same value in a custom property, and bare parentheses `calc((((var(--x) - 1px) - 1px)...)`.
evidence: perf scan on local master binding (debug build) and 1.33.0 release; repro.mjs on local, 1.33.0, 1.22.0 (all slow), 1.14.0 d16 252 ms (also slow). Code read of Calc::parse_value.

fix.approach: In Calc::parse_value, if the next token is a math function and Calc::parse failed, return the error instead of falling through to V::parse (PR #1390). Alternatively restructure so V::parse is only attempted for non-function tokens.

openPRs.assessment: Root-cause fix in Calc::parse_value: peeks for a math-function name and returns the Calc::parse error instead of retrying through V::parse. The name list matches the arms of Calc::parse_with today, but it is a second list to keep in sync (a shared helper would be safer). Reviewer should confirm no V::parse accepts a math function that Calc<V>::parse rejects (from reading, V::parse for Length/LengthPercentage/Angle etc. goes back through the same Calc<V>, so it should not). Has a depth-40 regression test and a mixed max/calc/min case. Codex review failed to run; no maintainer review yet. Not built.

draftReply:
Thanks, confirmed. On 1.33.0, `width: calc(calc(... var(--x) - 1px ...) - 1px)` takes 2.6 ms at 10 levels, 150 ms at 15 and 4.5 s at 20; it has behaved this way since at least 1.14.0. The cause is in math-function parsing: when a nested function can't be fully parsed because of `var()`, the same function is parsed a second time through another path, so the work doubles at each level. The output is still correct, only slow. Without `var()`, or in a custom property, the same nesting is instant.

There's an open PR, #1390, that addresses this. Until it's released, the workaround is to avoid feeding deeply nested generated `calc()`/`min()` around `var()` into typed properties.
